query: What company traits explain regional clustering?

per_column.name: primary_tech_domain
per_column.rationale: Well-separated, interpretable tech categories that plausibly vary by region (e.g., semiconductor vs fintech clustering); strong segmentation variable despite ~24% nulls.

per_column.name: industry_vertical
per_column.rationale: Human-readable industry categories external to region that can be grouped and compared; enterprise_software dominates but distribution still permits contrasts.

per_column.name: company_stage
per_column.rationale: Clear, balanced lifecycle categories (early/growth/established/investor); regional ecosystems differ markedly by stage, making this a rich exploratory axis.

per_column.name: target_market
per_column.rationale: Interpretable B2B/B2C segmentation; somewhat skewed toward b2b_enterprise but still allows meaningful cross-tabulation with region.

per_column.name: delivery_model
per_column.rationale: Distinct delivery categories (SaaS, services, hardware) that can reflect regional economic structure; well-labeled and groupable.

per_column.name: hardware_software_orientation
per_column.rationale: Interpretable orientation categories; partially overlaps delivery_model (hardware/software axis) but adds a clean binary-ish contrast useful for regional comparison.

judge.rationale: All six columns are external, associational, and framed as clean human-readable categorical segments rather than opaque scores, directly supporting exploration of which company traits co-vary with regional clustering. Categories are well-separated and groupable, and several (tech domain, stage, hardware/software) are classic regional-differentiator axes. Minor weaknesses: some skew (target_market, industry_vertical concentrate heavily in one bucket, limiting contrast) and partial redundancy between delivery_model and hardware_software_orientation. None merely restate the focus. Overall a strong EDA-oriented set.
